reason: E1 directly supports improved CO oxidation activity and stability with increasing disorder up to 7 metals. E2 and E3 confirm the solventless thermolysis synthesis using dithiocarbamate precursors and the production of 4- to 7-metal spinel oxides, but the cited synthesis temperature is 900 °C, not the 500–800 °C range specified in the hypothesis conditions.
premises: Increasing configurational disorder in spinel oxides improves CO oxidation activity (lower T10).
Higher configurational disorder improves long-term stability against deactivation.
Solventless thermolysis of metal dithiocarbamate precursors can synthesize multi-metal spinel oxides with uniform elemental distribution.
The synthesis method works at temperatures relevant to automotive exhaust (500–800 °C).
The benefits scale with the number of metals (up to 7) in the spinel oxide.
